taskSpec.name: HN AI Post Watcher
taskSpec.summary: For each new Hacker News post from the newest feed, classifies whether it is about AI/ML and, if so, produces a one-sentence 'why it matters' summary; otherwise tags it as skipped.
taskSpec.goal: Continuously monitor Hacker News newest posts and surface only AI/ML-related ones with a concise relevance summary, tagging all others as skipped.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Post title from the HN feed item
inputs.example: Show HN: I built an open-source RAG evaluation toolkit

inputs.name: link
inputs.description: URL of the post or linked article

inputs.name: summary
inputs.description: Feed item description/summary text (may be empty)
inputs.example: A CLI tool that scores retrieval pipelines on faithfulness and recall.

inputs.name: id
inputs.description: Unique feed item identifier for dedupe/tracking

outputs.name: is_ai_ml
outputs.description: True if the post is about AI or machine learning

outputs.name: why_it_matters
outputs.description: One-sentence summary of why the post matters; empty string when skipped

outputs.name: reason
outputs.description: Brief note on the classification decision (matched topics or why it was skipped)

steps: Read the incoming feed item fields (title, link, summary).

Classify the post as AI/ML-related by checking title and summary for AI/ML topics (LLMs, agents, RAG, training, models, ML frameworks, research, etc.), treating borderline hardware/business posts as relevant only if AI/ML is the core subject.
If relevant, write exactly one sentence explaining why the post matters (novelty, practical use, scale, or controversy), grounded only in the title/summary content.
If not relevant, set status to 'skipped' with an empty why_it_matters and a short reason.
Emit the structured output {is_ai_ml, status, why_it_matters, reason} for downstream delivery (e.g., to a log, sheet, or messaging channel).
constraints: Do not fetch the feed or the linked article; judge only from the provided title and summary.
why_it_matters must be a single sentence and under 40 words.
Never fabricate details not present in the item; if the summary is empty, base the summary on the title alone and note low confidence in reason.
Keep classification conservative: generic tech/business posts that merely mention AI in passing should be skipped.
Output must always include all four fields, even for skipped items.
successCriteria: Every output has status set to exactly 'relevant' or 'skipped' and is_ai_ml consistent with it.
For relevant items, why_it_matters is exactly one sentence, under 40 words, and references something concrete from the title or summary.
For skipped items, why_it_matters is empty and reason explains the exclusion.
No output contains information not derivable from the provided item fields.
assumptions: 'Every 2 minutes' means the platform polls the feed every 2 minutes and runs this agent once per new item; the agent itself does not fetch the feed.
AI/ML is interpreted broadly: LLMs, generative AI, ML research, frameworks, agents, and applied ML all count.
Output is delivered to a default downstream sink (log/notification) configured at deployment; delivery is out of scope for this agent.
Borderline posts (AI-adjacent hardware, funding news) are skipped unless AI/ML is the main subject.

exampleInputs.title: Show HN: I built an open-source RAG evaluation toolkit
exampleInputs.summary: A CLI tool that scores retrieval pipelines on faithfulness and recall.

exampleInputs.title: My favorite mechanical keyboards of 2025
exampleInputs.summary: A roundup of ten keyboards with sound tests.

exampleInputs.title: OpenAI releases new o-series model with improved reasoning

trigger.description: Platform polls https://hnrss.org/newest every 2 minutes, dedupes items, and runs this agent once per new feed item with the item's fields as inputs.

plan.rationale: Each feed item is independently classified as AI/ML-relevant or not, then only relevant items get a one-sentence 'why it matters' summary; skipped items get empty fields. A cheap decision node handles the conservative classification, an LLM writes the grounded sentence only on the relevant branch, and a merge + transform assembles the uniform four-field output. No web fetching is needed since the agent judges only from provided fields.

steps.purpose: Classify the post as AI/ML-related or not from {{input.title}} and {{input.summary}}, with a conservative rule: generic tech/business posts mentioning AI only in passing are not AI/ML. Question: 'Is this Hacker News post primarily about AI or machine learning (LLMs, agents, RAG, training, models, ML frameworks, research, applied ML)? Borderline AI-adjacent hardware/business posts count only if AI/ML is the core subject.' Options: relevant / skipped. Route on the answer.

On the 'relevant' branch, write exactly one sentence (under 40 words) explaining why the post matters (novelty, practical use, scale, or controversy), grounded strictly in {{input.title}} and {{input.summary}}; if the summary is empty, base it on the title alone.

Build the uniform output object: is_ai_ml = true and status='relevant' with why_it_matters from the LLM when the relevant branch ran; otherwise is_ai_ml=false, status='skipped', why_it_matters=''. reason comes from the decision node's explanation (matched topics, or why it was skipped / low confidence note when summary was empty).

plan.output: is_ai_ml (boolean, from the classification decision), status ('relevant' or 'skipped', from the classification), why_it_matters (one-sentence LLM summary on the relevant branch, empty string when skipped), reason (classification rationale from the decision node, including low-confidence note when summary was empty).

output.why_it_matters: This open-source CLI toolkit matters because it gives RAG developers a practical, standardized way to measure faithfulness and recall in retrieval pipelines, filling a common evaluation gap.

criteria.criterion: why_it_matters is exactly one sentence under 40 words referencing the RAG evaluation toolkit or retrieval pipelines

checks.actual: This open-source CLI toolkit matters because it gives RAG developers a practical, standardized way to measure faithfulness and recall in retrieval pipelines, filling a common evaluation gap.
